title: To Our Redeemer’s Glorious Name
description: To Our Redeemer’s Glorious Name in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Anne Steele wrote these words. They were printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 101.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: To our Re-deem-er’s glo-rious name A-wake the sa-cred song! O may His love, im-mor-tal flame, Tune ev-ery heart and tongue!

lines: O may His love, immortal flame,
His love, what mortal thought can reach!
He left His radiant throne on high,
Left the bright realms of bliss,
And came to earth to bleed and die,—
Dear Lord, while we adoring pay
May every heart with rapture say,
O may the sweet, the blissful theme
Till strangers love the charming name

licence: Public domain: Anne Steele died in 1778.
credits: Words by Anne Steele (1717–1778), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
